newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Tokyo stocks tumble on economic woes, Hong Kong up.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks tumble on economic woes, Hong Kong up.

text.p: Tokyo stocks tumbled 2.6 percent to their lowest level in a year on Thursday, hammered by deepening gloom about Japan's economic outlook.
Bangkok's market was another big loser, shedding almost 2.5 percent. Hong Kong shares however, managed modest gains.
Stock markets around Asia were generally mixed but Seoul was a clear winner, soaring nearly 4.5 percent on talk of heavy support from pension funds.
Tokyo's benchmark Nikkei average sagged a steep 2.6 percent, its third biggest drop this year, on accelerated selling after sinking through key psychological levels.
"Market sentiment was feeble to begin with as there are too many uncertainties surrounding the economy," said Yasuo Ueki, Nikko Securities general manager.

The Nikkei dipped below the 20,000 level during the morning and fell through another key floor at around 19,920 points before settling 522.36 points down at 19,570.67, its lowest close since December 21 last year.
Brokers cited growing worries about the Japanese economy, which is still struggling to reach full recovery despite low interest rates and the prop of public spending.
Hong Kong's Hang Seng index closed on a gain of 80.54 points or 0.63 percent at 12,846.56.
Selective strength in some major blue chips drove the upswing, but brokers said the overall tone during the session had been fairly subdued ahead of the holiday period.
"People are looking around for value," said Miles Remington, sales trader at Crosby Securities. Bangkok's SET Index closed at a new year low of 832.60, down 21.22 points or 2.49 percent.
Sales of blue chip stocks by foreigners during the morning session triggered forced selling orders by retail clients, which sent the battered market to that low, analysts said.
Bank stocks bore the brunt of selling, dragging the finance sector down a hefty 5.5 percent.
Seoul share prices however, rocketed a steep 4.47 percent, a gain of 29.58 points, to finish at 690.97.
Investors actively bought stocks, on speculation that public pension funds would buy heavily before the end of the year, brokers said.
It was the largest rise seen for the Seoul index this year.

Manila shares also ended in positive territory after surging to close 48.58 points, or 1.56 percent higher at 3,154.38 points as fund managers resorted to window-dressing and positioning for next year, said traders.
Bombay's market was another winner, marking four consecutive days of gains this week.
Local fund buying was aided by rumours that former finance minister Manmohan Singh might take over as chief of the Congress parliamentary party, traders said.
Bombay's main index ended up 34.37 points or 1.15 percent higher at 3035.61.
Selective buying lifted Kuala Lumpur share prices to a stronger finish. The Composite Index ended up 9.14 points or 0.77 percent to 1,201.03.
Singapore shares ended firmer on light bargain hunting in blue chips. The Straits Times Industrial index gained 3.57 points to 2,199.35.
Australia's All Ordinaries index closed eight points higher at 2,331.7, helped by a stronger U.S. share market overnight.
New Zealand shares however, sank 0.65 percent or 15.32 points to 2,335.91, pressured by losses in market heavyweight, Telecom.
Taiwan's weighted index finished 37.12 points or 0.54 percent lower at 6,859.40, off an intra-session high of 6,921.70, as institutional selling emerged to offset early gains, brokers said.
Jakarta share prices also slipped amid profit-taking in selected big-caps, brokers said.
The composite index ended down 1.13 points, or 0.18 percent, at 628.32 points.
SIMEX Brent crude futures dipped but brokers said they expected a rebound in the near term.
February Brent was last traded at US$23.84 per barrel, down eight cents from the London settlement on Wednesday.
Hong Kong gold ended unchanged at US$369.10/60 against New York's Wednesday close, after lacklustre trading, dealers said.
At 1118 GMT, the dollar was trading at 114.05/15 yen and 1.5560/64 marks after a range-bound Tokyo session.
